data.why: The dashboard only reads a pre-built DuckDB file (bronze/silver/gold tables normally populated by pipeline.py against live Open Targets/ChEMBL/UniProt APIs); since the run has no network access at start time and install can only reach PyPI/npm/GitHub, seed_db.py is placed at the pipeline's path and run once during install to build data/biomarker.duckdb directly with realistic synthetic values for two diseases (type II diabetes mellitus, breast carcinoma), including genes with missing UniProt enrichment and drugs with missing pChEMBL potency to exercise the dashboard's null-handling.

goals: Select a disease and identify its top-ranked therapeutic gene targets
Compare how genetic evidence, druggability, and evidence richness each contribute to a target's composite score
Prioritize Tier 1 targets over Tier 2/3 candidates for follow-up
Find which existing drugs already modulate a given target, their potency, and how far they've progressed in clinical trials
Drill into a specific gene's protein function, subcellular localization, and known disease associations
Compare the target landscape across two different diseases

review.summary: The tree matches the README's purpose closely (which genes are the best targets for a disease, and which drugs already hit them), with real stages, good general/specific wording and six well-cut features, and 10 of the 11 screens I checked match their nodes. Before filing, it needs the data source labelled as synthetic, the PNG-export citation corrected, the t1 branch fixed, and a few small wording and coverage changes.
